content.value_statement: Modern Vitest projects need clear testing patterns across configuration, mocks, coverage, and snapshots. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Vitest guidance for practical test work.
actual_capabilities: Explains Vitest configuration, CLI options, test APIs, suites, assertions, and hooks.
Guides mocking for functions, modules, timers, dates, environment values, and globals.
Covers snapshots, coverage settings, reporters, fixtures, filtering, tags, and benchmarks.
Documents advanced vi utilities, custom environments, type testing, and multi-project workspaces.
Highlights Vitest 4 and Vitest 5 behavior changes where the references include them.
limitations: It does not execute tests or inspect project files by itself.
It is based on generated Vitest 5.x beta reference material.
Examples may need changes for project-specific versions, plugins, and dependencies.
It does not replace official documentation for unstable beta behavior.

use_cases.title: Set Up Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Create practical Vitest tests with clear setup, assertions, hooks, and CLI choices.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Reliability
use_cases.description: Use mocking, fixtures, snapshots, filtering, and coverage guidance to reduce flaky test behavior.

use_cases.title: Maintain Monorepo Testing
use_cases.description: Plan Vitest projects, environment options, reporters, tags, and per-project configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vitest Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a first Vitest unit test for this function. Explain the test structure and useful assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Mocking
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to mock a module and environment value in Vitest. Include cleanup steps and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Vitest coverage needs and recommend settings for reporters, include patterns, excludes, and thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workspace Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Vitest workspace strategy for unit, integration, and browser tests across multiple packages.

output_examples.input: I need reliable DOM tests for a Vite application.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a browser-like environment, per-file environment control, setup cleanup, and focused assertions for DOM behavior.

output_examples.input: My snapshots fail differently in local runs and CI.
output_examples.output: The response explains update behavior, CI restrictions, obsolete snapshot handling, and a workflow for reviewing snapshot changes.

output_examples.input: Our monorepo needs separate unit and integration test settings.
output_examples.output: The response proposes Vitest projects, naming, include patterns, isolation choices, reporters, and per-project options.

best_practices: Use explicit setup and cleanup for mocks, globals, timers, and environment values.
Prefer focused test projects and filters for large repositories.
Keep coverage include, exclude, and threshold rules visible in configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not copy beta examples without checking your installed Vitest version.
Do not update snapshots blindly without reviewing the behavior change.
Do not rely on shared mutable state across isolated tests.

faq.question: Does this skill run Vitest tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an AI assistant can use while working in your project.

faq.question: Which Vitest version does it cover?
faq.answer: The references are based on Vitest 5.x beta material generated in June 2026.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from Jest?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Jest-compatible APIs, mocking patterns, snapshots, and configuration differences.

faq.question: Does it cover TypeScript tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TypeScript, type testing, expectTypeOf, and configuration guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with CI settings?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers run mode, reporters, snapshots in CI, tags, retries, and filtering patterns.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with secrets?
faq.answer: Use only test values in examples. Keep real credentials out of tests, snapshots, and shared prompts.
